diagnosis: HPV-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) arising on dVIN
legend: Keratinizing type of SCC (right side of the image) with keratin pearl formation arising from differentiated VIN (dVIN) lesion (left side of the image). This tumour was p16-negative.

diagnosis: HPV-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma arising on dVIN
legend: p53 immunohistochemistry. Tumoural cells showing strong and diffuse nuclear positivity (overexpression pattern). The molecular testing revealed missense TP53 mutation.

diagnosis: HPV-independent well-differentiated invasive squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) arising from vaVIN
legend: The invasive carcinoma displays verruciform, exophytic architecture, overlapping with subjacent vaVIN lesion. There is also prominent keratin pearl formation, a hallmark of well-differentiated SCC. The invasive nests are well-rounded. This tumour was p16-negative.

diagnosis: HPV-independent well-differentiated invasive squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) arising from vaVIN
legend: Despite being malignant, the tumour cells tend to have abundant eosinophylic cytoplasm and minimal atypia compared with poorly differentiated SCC.

diagnosis: HPV-independent well-differentiated invasive squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) arising from vaVIN
legend: p53 immunohistochemistry shows scattered heterogeneous staining in the tumoural cells, consistent with wildtype p53 pattern and suggestive of absence of TP53 mutation (confirmed by next-generation sequencing testing).

diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma, HPV-independent with "spray-like" pattern
legend: This tumour shows "spray-like" pattern characterized by a high degree of tumor cell dissociation, where individual cancer cells or small clusters infiltrate the surrounding stroma in a dispersed, non-cohesive manner. The stroma is markedly desmoplastic. This pattern is suggestive of epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Patients tend to have aggressive clinical outcome.
p53 immunohistochemistry shows null pattern: complete absence of staining in the tumoural cells, whereas inflammatory and stromal cells retain some degree of staining.
